on his own terms not as an inductive inference that the future will resemble the past, but as a non-inductive, methodological rule of 'conjectural risk-management': since we cannot know truth, we act on the theory that has survived the most severe tests because it has exposed itself to the highest risk of falsification and failed to be eliminated, thereby offering the best available (though fallible) guide for action without assigning it higher probability.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the preference implicitly assumes nature's uniformity to project past survival into future
